methodological_rigor.justification: This is a multicenter, prospective real-world cohort evaluating end-of-treatment ctDNA-MRD in uniformly treated first-line LBCL, with clear eligibility windows for EOT plasma and PET-CT timing (Methods; Patients). The study uses prespecified analysis references (statistical analysis plan in Data Supplement) and benchmarks MRD against IPI and PET-CT, including multivariable Cox models and discrimination metrics (Methods; Statistical Analyses). Key limitations are intrinsic to the noninterventional design and the lack of centrally reviewed PET-CT, which the authors acknowledge (Discussion; Limitations).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work addresses a common clinical problem in LBCL: limited PPV of end-of-treatment PET-CT and the need for better remission assessment (Abstract; Introduction). It is an individual prospective cohort study evaluating prognostic performance of ctDNA-MRD for PFS/OS, consistent with Oxford LoE 2b (Methods; Statistical Analyses). Findings could inform near-term response assessment strategies, though interventional utility is explicitly stated as unproven without prospective MRD-directed trials (Discussion).

reporting_quality.justification: As a prospective observational cohort, STROBE is the relevant framework, and the manuscript reports cohort selection, timing constraints, endpoints (PFS/OS), and key analytic approaches (Methods; Statistical Analyses; Figures). The text repeatedly points to a Data Supplement for full protocol, prespecified SAP, specimen processing/bioinformatics details, and additional tables/figures (Methods). While this supports transparency, the normalized main text does not include an explicit public data/code sharing statement, so reproducibility artifacts appear partial from the provided document.

novelty_literature.justification: The manuscript prospectively validates ultrasensitive PhasED-Seq ctDNA-MRD at end of first-line therapy in a national, uniformly treated, multicenter LBCL cohort, addressing limitations of prior smaller or heterogeneous studies (Abstract; Introduction). It provides quantitative comparisons versus PET-CT (PPV/NPV) and demonstrates independent prognostic value in multivariate models (Abstract; Results). This represents a substantial extension toward real-world validation rather than a purely incremental replication.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly structured with standard sections and provides concrete quantitative effect estimates (HRs, CIs, P values) in the Abstract and Results. Methods and endpoint definitions are described with operational timing windows and analytic methods (Methods; Statistical Analyses). Some critical details are deferred to the Data Supplement, but the main narrative remains readable and logically organized.

key_strengths: Prospective, multicenter real-world cohort with uniform first-line treatment and clearly defined EOT sampling/imaging windows.
Strong and consistent prognostic separation for PFS/OS by EOT ctDNA-MRD with multivariable analyses versus IPI and PET-CT.
Clinically relevant benchmarking of MRD performance against PET-CT (including PPV/NPV comparisons).
key_concerns: Observational design limits causal claims and immediate treatment-actionability; authors note MRD-directed escalation is not yet proven.
EOT PET-CT was not centrally reviewed, introducing potential interpretation variability.
Key protocol/SAP and bioinformatics implementation details reside in the Data Supplement and are not fully recoverable from the normalized main text.
No explicit public data/code sharing statement is visible in the normalized manuscript.
chief_reviewer.rationale: Methodologically solid prospective validation with high clinical relevance, but as a noninterventional prognostic cohort it sits below the very top tier and reads as a strong tier-2 biomarker-validation paper pending broader implementation and interventional confirmation.
